title: Tilt-controlled Drude anisotropy in nodal-line semimetals: logarithmic enhancement, interband correction, gauge consistency, and the Landau-damping window
abstract: We study the anisotropic charge response of a three-dimensional tilted nodal-line semimetal in which the tilt enters the spectrum through an identity term and acts as the model control parameter. Using the Kubo formula with line-integral vertices, we show that the tilt-induced deformation of the low-energy phase space produces parametrically different longitudinal and transverse Drude responses: the longitudinal weight grows logarithmically as $D_{zz}=B\ln(1/δ)$ with the analytically determined coefficient $B=g/(2π)^2$---within the window in which the Fermi-surface tail lies inside the ultraviolet cutoff, while at a fixed physical cutoff the weight saturates instead at a cutoff-set plateau---whereas the transverse weight follows a stronger algebraic scaling $D_\perp\simδ^{-1}$; the leading $\sqrtδ$ corrections to both asymptotic forms are obtained analytically. The interband polarization retains the $q^2$ long-wavelength structure, with a coefficient that is infrared-integrable through Pauli blocking at finite doping yet carries a slow ultraviolet logarithm; it renormalizes the collective mode multiplicatively and sets the interband absorption threshold $ω_c=2μ/(1+|η_z|)$. A self-consistent solution of the plasmon dispersion identifies a tilt-dependent damping-free window bounded by the interband continuum. We predict that the type-II extension of this window, within the stated bandwidth (Brillouin-zone-like) cutoff regularization, contains a candidate low-frequency acoustic-like branch outside the particle--hole continua for $η_z\gtrsim1.2$ over a finite window in momentum transfer.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the charge transport and collective excitations in a 3D tilted nodal-line semimetal. It finds that the longitudinal Drude weight shows a logarithmic enhancement due to the tilt, and furthermore, it predicts the existence of a low-frequency, damping-free acoustic-like plasmon branch when the tilt exceeds a critical value. The methodology involves advanced calculations using the Kubo formula and RPA for the dielectric function.
main_problem: The study investigates the anisotropic charge response (Drude and interband polarization) in a three-dimensional tilted nodal-line semimetal.
main_result: The longitudinal Drude weight exhibits a logarithmic enhancement, while the system predicts a low-frequency, damping-free acoustic-like plasmon branch in the type-II tilt regime.
method: The analysis employs the Kubo formula with line-integral vertices to calculate the charge response tensor, followed by a self-consistent solution for the plasmon dispersion relation.
model_or_system: The system is a 3D tilted nodal-line semimetal modeled by the Parallel-Tilted Nodal-Ring (PTNR) Hamiltonian, which includes a tilt parameter ($\eta z$) acting as a control parameter.
key_observables: Longitudinal Drude weight ($D_{zz}$), transverse Drude weight ($D_{\perp}$), interband polarization ($P_2$), and the plasmon dispersion $\omega_p(\mathbf{q})$.
important_parameters: Tilt parameter ($\eta z$), doping ($\mu$), and the momentum transfer ($\mathbf{q}$); the analysis distinguishes between type-I and type-II tilt regimes.
main_assumptions: The calculations rely on the Kubo formula, use a matched-asymptotics scheme for the long-tail integration, and the type-II results are stated within a specific Brillouin-zone regularization.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the Fermi-surface geometry, showing the tilted ring and the asymmetric integration interval used for the Drude weight calculation.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the anisotropic Drude response (longitudinal vs. transverse) using the Kubo formula, then incorporates the interband polarization, and finally solves the RPA condition to identify the plasmon dispersion and the resulting damping-free window.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of collective excitations and the emergence of gapless modes in topological semimetals provides theoretical insights into screening and low-energy dynamics, which are foundational concepts in many-body physics relevant to AMO and quantum optics.
